### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.deps

### Question

What I'm trying to do is to install the nvim-treesitter plugin and, synchronously, install parsers with it:

```lua
require("mini.deps").setup()
local add, now, later = MiniDeps.add, MiniDeps.now, MiniDeps.later

add {
	source = "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter",
	checkout = "main",
	hooks = {
		post_install = function() require("nvim-treesitter").install({ "stable", "unstable" }):wait() end,
	},
}
```

And I'm getting the error:

```text
(mini.deps) Error executing post_install hook in `nvim-treesitter`:
/home/nicolas/.config/nvim/init.lua:108: module 'nvim-treesitter' not found:
...
```

I wrapped the installation of parses with `later` and it worked. But that's not what I originally intended.

The question is: shouldn't I be able to require the plugin I'm just installing in the post_install hook?

comment_data.body:
> I wrapped the installation of parses with `later` and it worked. But that's not what I originally intended.
> 
> The question is: shouldn't I be able to require the plugin I'm just installing in the post_install hook?

That's a good question. The observed behavior is because all plugins are installed before executing `:packadd` on them. So installation has finished (i.e. `post_install` hook is executed) before Neovim itself "knows" about the installed plugin.

I'll think about whether it is a good idea to trigger `post_install` *after* `:packadd` or indeed documenting the `later` approach (which I also have been using in my config) is better here.

To strictly some code strictly executed just after install (and not in `later()` which will be executed way later), the workaround is to have `post_install` set some boolean flag and conditionally execute some code afterwards. So something like this:

```lua
local nvim_treesitter_installed = false
add({
  source = 'nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter',
  checkout = 'main',
  hooks = { post_install = function() nvim_treesitter_installed = true end },
})

if nvim_treesitter_installed then require('nvim-treesitter').install({ 'stable', 'unstable' }) end
```

Got it.

> I'll think about whether it is a good idea to trigger `post_install` _after_ `:packadd`

It would make my setup more elegant, but I guess there's the use case where people change the plugin's code programmatically inside the hook (applying a patch or something) and want the plugin to be sourced only afterward. 

Maybe add a new hook after the `:packadd` or add a new flag like `run_packadd_before_hook`. Just throwing some ideas.

> To strictly some code strictly executed just after install (and not in later() which will be executed way later), the workaround is to have post_install set some boolean flag and conditionally execute some code afterwards

Hmm, I didn't think about that, good solution. But you gave me another idea. For now, I think I will just do:

```lua
require("mini.deps").setup()
local add, now, later = MiniDeps.add, MiniDeps.now, MiniDeps.later

add {
	source = "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter",
	checkout = "main",
	hooks = {
		post_install = function(args)
			vim.cmd("packadd " .. args.name)
			require("nvim-treesitter").install({ "stable", "unstable" }):wait()
		end,
	},
}
```

It seems to work. Do you foresee any problems that this may cause?
